children.text: Chapter 1
asāv ādityo na vyarocata
children.translated_text: That <s>Aditya</s> did not shine forth.

children.text: tasmai devāḥ prāyaścittim aicchan
children.translated_text: For him the gods sought an expiation.

children.text: tasmā etāṃ daśarṣabhām ālabhanta tayaivāsmin rucam adadhuḥ
children.translated_text: For him they seized this ten-bull offering; by that very offering they placed radiance in him.

children.text: yo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ syāt tasmā etāṃ daśarṣabhām ālabheta
children.translated_text: If one should desire brahmavarcasa (sacred brilliance), he should seize this ten-bull offering for him.

children.text: amum evādityaṃ svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati
children.translated_text: He approaches that very <s>Aditya</s> with his own allotted share.

children.text: sa evāsmin brahmavarcasaṃ dadhāti
children.translated_text: He himself places brahmavarcasa in him.

children.text: brahmavarcasy eva bhavati
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of brahmavarcasa.

children.text: vasantā prātas trīṃllalāmān ālabheta grīṣme madhyaṃdine ||
children.translated_text: In spring, in the morning, he should seize three with marked foreheads; in summer, at midday,

children.text: śitipṛṣṭhāṁ śarady aparāhṇe trīñchitivārān
children.translated_text: three with white backs; in autumn, in the afternoon, three with white variegations.

children.text: trīṇi vā ādityasya tejāṃsi vasantā prātar grīṣme madhyaṃdine śarady aparāhṇe
children.translated_text: For there are three radiances of <s>Aditya</s>: spring in the morning, summer at midday, and autumn in the afternoon.

children.text: yāvanty eva tejāṃsi tānyevāvarunddhe
children.translated_text: As many radiances as there are, those very ones he secures.

children.text: trayastraya ālabhyante
children.translated_text: They are seized three by three.

children.text: abhipūrvam evāsmin tejo dadhāti
children.translated_text: He places radiance in him in proper forward order.

children.text: saṃvatsaram paryālabhyante
children.translated_text: They are seized around the year.

children.text: saṃvatsaro vai brahmavarcasasya pradātā
children.translated_text: For the year is the giver of brahmavarcasa.

children.text: saṃvatsara evāsmai brahmavarcasam prayacchati
children.translated_text: In the year itself it bestows brahmavarcasa upon him.

children.text: brahmavarcasy eva bhavati
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of brahmavarcasa.

children.text: saṃvatsarasya parastāt prājāpatyaṃ kadrum ||
children.translated_text: After the year, he should seize for <s>Prajapati</s> a brown one

children.text: ālabheta
children.translated_text: as the offering.

children.text: prajāpatiḥ sarvā devatāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajapati</s> is all the deities.

children.text: devatāsu eva pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: He becomes established among the deities themselves.

children.text: yadi bibhīyāt
children.translated_text: If he should fear,

children.text: duścarmā bhaviṣyāmīti somāpauṣṇaṃ śyāmam ālabheta
children.translated_text: 'I shall become bad-skinned,' he should seize a dark animal for <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pusan</s>.

children.text: saumyo vai devatayā puruṣaḥ pauṣṇāḥ paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: A man is Saumya by deity, and cattle belong to <s>Pusan</s>.

children.text: svayaivāsmai devatayā paśubhis tvacaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: By his own deity, together with cattle, he makes skin for him.

children.text: na duścarmā bhavati
children.translated_text: He does not become bad-skinned.

children.text: devāś ca vai yamaś cāsmiṃlloke 'spardhanta
children.translated_text: The gods and <s>Yama</s> once competed in this world.

children.text: sa yamo devānām indriyaṃ vīryam ayuvata
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yama</s> took away the gods' power and strength.

children.text: tad yamasya ||
children.translated_text: That was <s>Yama</s>'s

children.text: yamatvam
children.translated_text: Yama-hood.

children.text: te devā amanyanta
children.translated_text: The gods thought,

children.text: yamo vā idam abhūd yad vayaṃ sma iti
children.translated_text: 'This has become <s>Yama</s>, whereas it was we.'

children.text: te prajāpatim upādhāvan
children.translated_text: They approached <s>Prajapati</s>.

children.text: sa etau prajāpatir ātmana ukṣavaśau niramimīta
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajapati</s> created from himself these two, a bull and a barren cow.

children.text: te devā vaiṣṇāvaruṇīṃ vaśām ālabhantaindram ukṣāṇam
children.translated_text: The gods seized the barren cow for <s>Vishnu</s> and <s>Varuna</s>, and the bull for <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: taṃ varuṇenaiva grāhayitvā viṣṇunā yajñena prāṇudantaindreṇaivāsyendriyam avṛñjata
children.translated_text: Having seized him with <s>Varuna</s>, they drove him away by <s>Vishnu</s>, by the sacrifice, and with <s>Indra</s> they took his power.

children.text: yo bhrātṛvyavānt syāt sa spardhamāno vaiṣṇāvaruṇīm ||
children.translated_text: If one has a rival, while competing he should seize for <s>Vishnu</s> and <s>Varuna</s>

children.text: vaśām ālabhetaindram ukṣāṇam
children.translated_text: a barren cow, and for <s>Indra</s> a bull.

children.text: varuṇenaiva bhrātṛvyaṃ grāhayitvā viṣṇunā yajñena praṇudate aindreṇaivāsyendriyaṃ vṛṅkte
children.translated_text: Having seized the rival with <s>Varuna</s>, he drives him away by <s>Vishnu</s>, by the sacrifice, and with what belongs to <s>Indra</s> he takes his power.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati
children.translated_text: He prospers in himself, and his rival is driven away.

children.text: indro vṛtram ahan
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vritra</s>.

children.text: taṃ vṛtro hataḥ ṣoḍaśabhir bhogair asināt
children.translated_text: When slain, <s>Vritra</s> bound him with sixteen coils.

children.text: tasya vṛtrasya śīrṣato gāva udāyan
children.translated_text: From <s>Vritra</s>'s head cattle came forth.

children.text: tā vaidehyo 'bhavan
children.translated_text: They became the Vaidehī cows.

children.text: tāsām ṛṣabho jaghane 'nūdait
children.translated_text: Their bull came forth afterwards from the rear.

children.text: tam indraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>

children.text: acāyat
children.translated_text: noticed him.

children.text: so 'manyata
children.translated_text: He thought,

children.text: yo vā imam ālabheta mucyetāsmāt pāpmana iti
children.translated_text: 'Whoever would seize this one would be released from this evil.'

children.text: sa āgneyaṃ kṛṣṇagrīvam ālabhataindram ṛṣabham
children.translated_text: He seized a black-necked animal for <s>Agni</s> and a bull for <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tasyāgnir eva svena bhāgadheyenopasṛtaḥ ṣoḍaśadhā vṛtrasya bhogān apy adahad aindreṇendriyam ātmann adhatta
children.translated_text: Then <s>Agni</s>, approached with his own allotted share, burned up <s>Vritra</s>'s sixteenfold coils, and by what belonged to <s>Indra</s> he placed power in himself.

children.text: yaḥ pāpmanā gṛhītaḥ syāt sa āgneyaṃ kṛṣṇagrīvam ālabhetaindram ṛṣabham
children.translated_text: If one is seized by evil, he should seize a black-necked animal for <s>Agni</s> and a bull for <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: agnir evāsya svena bhāgadheyenopasṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, approached with his own allotted share,

children.text: pāpmānam apidahaty aindreṇendriyam ātman dhatte
children.translated_text: burns up his evil, and by what belongs to <s>Indra</s> he places power in himself.

children.text: mucyate pāpmanaḥ
children.translated_text: He is released from evil.

children.text: bhavaty eva
children.translated_text: He indeed prospers.

children.text: dyāvāpṛthivyāṃ dhenum ālabheta jyogaparuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: One who has long been excluded should seize a milch cow for Heaven and Earth.

children.text: anayor hi vā eṣo 'pratiṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: For he is not established in these two.

children.text: athaiṣa jyog aparuddho dyāvāpṛthivī eva svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati
children.translated_text: Then this one, long excluded, approaches Heaven and Earth themselves with their own allotted share.

children.text: te evainam pratiṣṭhāṃ gamayataḥ
children.translated_text: They bring him to establishment.

children.text: praty eva tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: He stands firmly again.

children.text: paryāriṇī bhavati
children.translated_text: She should be one that has gone around.

children.text: paryārīva hy etasya rāṣṭraṃ yo jyogaparuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: For the kingdom of one who has long been excluded is, as it were, gone around him.

children.text: samṛddhyai
children.translated_text: This is for prosperity.

children.text: vāyavyam ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Vayu</s>

children.text: vatsam ālabheta
children.translated_text: he should seize a calf.

children.text: vāyur vā anayor vatsaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Vayu</s> is the calf of these two.

children.text: ime vā etasmai lokā apaśuṣkā viḍ apaśuṣkā
children.translated_text: For him these worlds are dried up, and the people are dried up.

children.text: athaiṣa jyog aparuddho vāyum eva svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati
children.translated_text: Then this one, long excluded, approaches <s>Vayu</s> himself with his own allotted share.

children.text: sa evāsmā imāṃllokān viśam pradāpayati
children.translated_text: He causes these worlds and the people to be made fruitful for him.

children.text: prāsmā ime lokāḥ snuvanti
children.translated_text: These worlds flow forth for him.

children.text: bhuñjaty enaṃ viḍ upatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: He enjoys them; the people attend upon him.

children.text: Chapter 2
āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped abhicarant sarasvaty ājyabhāgā syād bārhaspatyaś caruḥ
children.translated_text: When performing an abhicaric rite, he should offer an eleven-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>; <s>Sarasvati</s> should have the butter-portions, and there should be a caru for <s>Brihaspati</s>.

children.text: yad āgnāvaiṣṇava ekādaśakapālo bhavati
children.translated_text: When there is an eleven-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>,

children.text: agniḥ sarvā devatā viṣṇur yajño devatābhiś caivainaṃ yajñena cābhicarati
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is all the deities and <s>Vishnu</s> is the sacrifice; with the deities and with the sacrifice he performs hostile magic against him.

children.text: sarasvaty ājyabhāgā bhavati vāg vai sarasvatī vācaivainam abhicarati
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvati</s> has the butter-portions; speech indeed is <s>Sarasvati</s>, and by speech he performs hostile magic against him.

children.text: bārhaspatyaś carur bhavati brahma vai devānām bṛhaspatir brahmaṇaivainam abhicarati ||
children.translated_text: There is a caru for <s>Brihaspati</s>; <s>Brihaspati</s> is the sacred formulation of the gods, and by the sacred formulation he performs hostile magic against him.

children.text: prati vai parastād abhicarantam abhicaranti
children.translated_text: Indeed, one who performs hostile magic is in turn assailed from beyond.

children.text: dve dve puronuvākye kuryād ati prayuktyai
children.translated_text: He should make two preliminary verses each, for excessive application.

children.text: etayaiva yajetābhicaryamāṇo devatābhir eva devatāḥ praticarati yajñena yajñaṃ vācā vācam brahmaṇā brahma sa devatāś caiva yajñaṃ ca madhyato vyavasarpati tasya na kutaścanopāvyādho bhavati
children.translated_text: With this very rite one who is being assailed by hostile magic should sacrifice: with the deities he counters the deities, with the sacrifice the sacrifice, with speech speech, with the sacred formulation the sacred formulation. He slips between both the deities and the sacrifice; no wound from anywhere comes near him.

children.text: nainam abhicarant stṛṇute
children.translated_text: The one performing hostile magic against him does not overcome him.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped yaṃ yajño na ||
children.translated_text: He for whom the sacrifice does not bow should offer an eleven-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>.

children.text: agniḥ sarvā devatā viṣṇur yajño 'gniṃ caiva viṣṇuṃ ca svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tāv evāsmai yajñam prayacchata upainaṃ yajño namati
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is all the deities and <s>Vishnu</s> is the sacrifice; he approaches <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s> with their own allotted share. They bestow the sacrifice upon him; the sacrifice bows to him.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ ghṛte caruṃ nirvapec cakṣuṣkāmaḥ
children.translated_text: One who desires sight should offer a ghee caru for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>.

children.text: agner vai cakṣuṣā manuṣyā vipaśyanti yajñasya devā agniṃ caiva viṣṇuṃ ca svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati
children.translated_text: With the eye of <s>Agni</s>, men see clearly. For the sacrifice, the gods approach <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s> themselves with their own allotted share.

children.text: tāv eva ||
children.translated_text: Those two indeed

children.text: asmiñcakṣur dhattaś cakṣuṣmān eva bhavati
children.translated_text: place sight in him here; he becomes possessed of sight.

children.text: dhenvai vā etad reto yad ājyam anaḍuhas taṇḍulā mithunād evāsmai cakṣuḥ prajanayati
children.translated_text: Ghee is the seed of the milch cow, and the rice-grains are of the bull. From a pair he thus generates sight for him.

children.text: ghṛte bhavati tejo vai ghṛtaṃ tejaś cakṣus tejasaivāsmai tejaś cakṣur avarunddhe
children.translated_text: It is in ghee. Ghee is brilliance, and brilliance is sight. By brilliance itself he secures brilliant sight for him.

children.text: indriyaṃ vai vīryaṃ vṛṅkte bhrātṛvyo yajamāno 'yajamānasyādhvarakalpām pratinirvaped bhrātṛvye yajamāne nāsyendriyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: The rival who is the sacrificer takes away the sense-power and vigor of the non-sacrificer. He should make a counter-offering to the adhvara-kalpa when the rival is sacrificing; he does not take away his sense-power

children.text: vīryaṃ vṛṅkte
children.translated_text: and vigor.

children.text: purā vācaḥ pravaditor nirvaped yāvaty eva vāk tām aproditām bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte tām asya vācam pravadantīm anyā vāco 'nupravadanti tā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ yajamāne dadhati
children.translated_text: He should offer before speech has been uttered. Whatever speech there is, he takes that unuttered speech of the rival. Other voices follow that speech of his as it is uttered; they place sense-power and vigor in the sacrificer.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet prātaḥsavanasyākāle sarasvaty ājyabhāgā syād bārhaspatyaś caruḥ
children.translated_text: At the wrong time for the morning pressing he should offer an eight-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>; <s>Sarasvati</s> should have the butter-portions, and there should be a caru for <s>Brihaspati</s>.

children.text: yad aṣṭākapālo bhavaty aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī gāyatram prātaḥsavanam prātaḥsavanam eva tenāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Because it is an eight-cup cake, and the <s>Gayatri</s> has eight syllables, and the morning pressing belongs to the <s>Gayatri</s>, by that he obtains the morning pressing itself.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapen mādhyaṃdinasya savanasyākāle sarasvaty ājyabhāgā syād bārhaspatyaś caruḥ
children.translated_text: At the wrong time for the midday pressing he should offer an eleven-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>; <s>Sarasvati</s> should have the butter-portions, and there should be a caru for <s>Brihaspati</s>.

children.text: yad ekādaśakapālo bhavaty ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭup traiṣṭubham mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam mādhyaṃdinam eva savanaṃ tenāpnoti
children.translated_text: Because it is an eleven-cup cake, and the <s>Trishtubh</s> has eleven syllables, and the midday pressing belongs to the <s>Trishtubh</s>, by that he obtains the midday pressing itself.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet tṛtīyasavanasyākāle sarasvaty ājyabhāgā syād bārhaspatyaś caruḥ
children.translated_text: At the wrong time for the third pressing he should offer a twelve-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>; <s>Sarasvati</s> should have the butter-portions, and there should be a caru for <s>Brihaspati</s>.

children.text: yad dvādaśakapālo bhavati dvādaśākṣarā jagatī jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ tṛtīyasavanam eva tenāpnoti
children.translated_text: Because it is a twelve-cup cake, and the <s>Jagati</s> has twelve syllables, and the third pressing belongs to the <s>Jagati</s>, by that he obtains the third pressing itself.

children.text: devatābhir eva devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the deities themselves he goes after the deities,

children.text: praticarati yajñena yajñaṃ vācā vācam brahmaṇā brahma kapālair eva chandāṃsy āpnoti puroḍāśaiḥ savanāni
children.translated_text: with sacrifice after sacrifice, with speech after speech, with brahman after brahman. By the potsherds themselves he obtains the metres, and by the sacrificial cakes the pressings.

children.text: maitrāvaruṇam ekakapālaṃ nirvaped vaśāyai kāle
children.translated_text: At the time for the barren cow he should offer a single-cup cake for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuna</s>.

children.text: yaivāsau bhrātṛvyasya vaśānubandhyā so evaiṣaitasyaikakapālo bhavati na hi kapālaiḥ paśum arhaty āptum ||
children.translated_text: That barren cow which is to be tied for the rival is the very same as this single-cup cake for him; for one cannot obtain an animal by means of potsherds.

children.text: Chapter 3
dhruvo 'si dhruvo 'haṃ sajāteṣu bhūyāsaṃ dhīraś cettā vasuvit
children.translated_text: 'You are firm; may I be firm among my kinsmen, steadfast, mindful, a winner of wealth.'

children.text: dhruvo 'si dhruvo 'haṃ sajāteṣu bhūyāsam ugraś cettā vasuvid
children.translated_text: 'You are firm; may I be firm among my kinsmen, fierce, mindful, a winner of wealth.'

children.text: dhruvo 'si dhruvo 'haṃ sajāteṣu bhūyāsam abhibhūś cettā vasuvit
children.translated_text: 'You are firm; may I be firm among my kinsmen, overpowering, mindful, a winner of wealth.'

children.text: āmanam asy āmanasya devā ye sajātāḥ kumārāḥ samanasas tān ahaṃ kāmaye hṛdā te māṃ kāmayantāṃ hṛdā tān ma āmanasaḥ kṛdhi svāhā
children.translated_text: 'You are attraction. Of attraction are the gods. Those boys who are kinsmen and of one mind, I desire them with my heart. May they desire me with their heart. Make them of one mind with me. Svaha.'

children.text: āmanam asi ||
children.translated_text: 'You are attraction.'

children.text: āmanasya devā yā striyaḥ samanasas tā ahaṃ kāmaye hṛdā tā māṃ kāmayantāṃ hṛdā tā ma āmanasaḥ kṛdhi svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Of attraction are the gods. Those women who are of one mind, I desire them with my heart. May they desire me with their heart. Make them of one mind with me. Svaha.'

children.text: vaiśvadevīṃ sāṃgrahaṇīṃ nirvaped grāmakāmaḥ
children.translated_text: One who desires a village should offer the <s>Vaishvadevi</s> sāṃgrahaṇī oblation.

children.text: vaiśvadevā vai sajātāḥ
children.translated_text: The kinsmen are indeed connected with all the gods.

children.text: viśvān eva devānt svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati
children.translated_text: He approaches all the gods themselves with their own allotted share.

children.text: ta evāsmai sajātān prayacchanti
children.translated_text: They bestow the kinsmen upon him.

children.text: grāmy eva bhavati
children.translated_text: He becomes a village-holder.

children.text: sāṃgrahaṇī bhavati
children.translated_text: It is sāṃgrahaṇī, a gathering oblation.

children.text: manograhaṇaṃ vai saṃgrahaṇam
children.translated_text: For gathering is the grasping of the mind.

children.text: mana eva sajātānām ||
children.translated_text: It grasps the mind itself of the kinsmen,

children.text: gṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: indeed.

children.text: dhruvo 'si dhruvo 'haṃ sajāteṣu bhūyāsam iti paridhīn paridadhāti
children.translated_text: Saying, 'You are firm; may I be firm among my kinsmen,' he sets the enclosing-sticks around.

children.text: āśiṣam evaitām āśāste
children.translated_text: He thereby asks for this blessing.

children.text: atho etad eva sarvaṃ sajāteṣv adhibhavati yasyaivaṃ viduṣa ete paridhayaḥ paridhīyante
children.translated_text: Moreover, all this becomes superior among the kinsmen of the one who knows thus, when these enclosing-sticks are set around.

children.text: āmanam asy āmanasya devā iti tisra āhutīr juhoti
children.translated_text: Saying, 'You are attraction; of attraction are the gods,' he offers three oblations.

children.text: etāvanto vai sajātā ye mahānto ye kṣullakā yā striyaḥ
children.translated_text: So many are the kinsmen: those who are great, those who are small, and the women.

children.text: tān evāvarunddhe
children.translated_text: He thereby secures them.

children.text: ta enam avaruddhā upatiṣṭhante ||
children.translated_text: Secured, they attend upon him.

children.text: Chapter 4
rāṣṭrakāmāya hotavyā rāṣṭraṃ vai rāṣṭrabhṛto rāṣṭreṇaivāsmai rāṣṭram avarunddhe rāṣṭram eva bhavati
children.translated_text: It should be offered for one who desires rulership. The rāṣṭrabhṛts are rulership; with rulership itself he secures rulership for him. He becomes rulership itself.

children.text: ātmane hotavyā rāṣṭraṃ vai rāṣṭrabhṛto rāṣṭram prajā rāṣṭram paśavo rāṣṭraṃ yac chreṣṭho bhavati rāṣṭreṇaiva rāṣṭram avarunddhe vasiṣṭhaḥ samānānām bhavati
children.translated_text: It should be offered for oneself. The rāṣṭrabhṛts are rulership: rulership is offspring, rulership is cattle, rulership is whatever is best. With rulership itself he secures rulership. He becomes the most excellent among his equals.

children.text: grāmakāmāya hotavyā rāṣṭraṃ vai rāṣṭrabhṛto rāṣṭraṃ sajātā rāṣṭreṇaivāsmai rāṣṭraṃ sajātān avarunddhe grāmī ||
children.translated_text: It should be offered for one who desires a village. The rāṣṭrabhṛts are rulership; rulership is the kinsmen. With rulership itself he secures rulership and the kinsmen for him. A village-holder

children.text: eva bhavati
children.translated_text: he indeed becomes.

children.text: adhidevane juhoty adhidevana evāsmai sajātān avarunddhe ta enam avaruddhā upatiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: He offers on the gaming-board; on the gaming-board itself he secures the kinsmen for him. Secured, they attend upon him.

children.text: rathamukha ojaskāmasya hotavyā ojo vai rāṣṭrabhṛta ojo ratha ojasaivāsmā ojo 'varunddha ojasvy eva bhavati
children.translated_text: For one desiring vigor, it should be offered at the front of the chariot. The rāṣṭrabhṛt is vigor, and the chariot is vigor. With vigor itself he secures vigor for him. He becomes vigorous indeed.

children.text: yo rāṣṭrād apabhūtaḥ syāt tasmai hotavyā yāvanto 'sya rathāḥ syus tān brūyād yuṅgdhvam iti rāṣṭram evāsmai yunakti ||
children.translated_text: It should be offered for one who has fallen away from rulership. As many chariots as he has, he should say of them, 'Yoke them.' He thereby yokes rulership itself for him.

children.text: āhutayo vā etasyākﾱptā yasya rāṣṭraṃ na kalpate svarathasya dakṣiṇaṃ cakram pravṛhya nāḍīm abhijuhuyād āhutīr evāsya kalpayati tā asya kalpamānā rāṣṭram anukalpate
children.translated_text: The oblations of one whose rulership is not established are unarranged. Having removed the right wheel of his own chariot, he should offer into the nave; he thereby arranges his oblations. As they become arranged for him, rulership becomes arranged for him accordingly.

children.text: saṃgrāme saṃyatte hotavyā rāṣṭraṃ vai rāṣṭrabhṛto rāṣṭre khalu vā ete vyāyacchante ye saṃgrāmaṃ saṃyanti yasya pūrvasya juhvati sa eva bhavati jayati taṃ saṃgrāmaṃ māndhuka idhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When battle is joined, offerings should be made. The Rāṣṭrabhṛt formulas are indeed royal power; surely those who join battle contend for royal power. Whichever side he offers for first, that side comes to be the one that wins that battle. The fuel is from the māndhuka tree.

children.text: bhavaty aṅgārā eva prativeṣṭamānā amitrāṇām asya senām prativeṣṭayanti
children.translated_text: There are coals turning round; they turn round and envelop the army of his enemies.

children.text: ya unmādyet tasmai hotavyā gandharvāpsaraso vā etam unmādayanti ya unmādyaty ete khalu vai gandharvāpsaraso yad rāṣṭrabhṛtas tasmai svāhā tābhyaḥ svāheti juhoti tenaivaināñchamayati
children.translated_text: For one who becomes mad, offerings should be made. The <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s> drive mad the man who becomes mad; and these Rāṣṭrabhṛts are indeed the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>. He offers, 'Svāhā to him, svāhā to them.' By that very means he pacifies them.

children.text: naiyagrodha audumbara āśvatthaḥ plākṣa itīdhmo bhavaty ete vai gandharvāpsarasāṃ gṛhāḥ sva evainān ||
children.translated_text: The fuel is from the nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, and plakṣa trees. These are indeed the homes of the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>; in their own

children.text: āyatane śamayati
children.translated_text: place he pacifies them.

children.text: abhicaratā pratilomaṃ hotavyāḥ prāṇān evāsya pratīcaḥ pratiyauti taṃ tato yena kena ca stṛṇute
children.translated_text: When performing hostile magic, the offerings should be made in reverse order. He drives the breaths of that man backward against him; then he fells him by whatever means he can.

children.text: svakṛta iriṇe juhoti pradare vaitad vā asyai nirṛtigṛhītaṃ nirṛtigṛhīta evainaṃ nirṛtyā grāhayati yad vācaḥ krūram tena vaṣaṭkaroti vāca evainaṃ krūreṇa pravṛścati tājag ārtim ārchati
children.translated_text: He offers on a self-made barren spot, or in a cleft. This place is seized by <s>Nirṛti</s>; in what is seized by <s>Nirṛti</s> he causes that man to be seized by <s>Nirṛti</s>. With what is cruel in speech he makes the vaṣaṭ-call; by the cruelty of speech he cuts him off. At once he falls into distress.

children.text: yasya kāmayetānnādyam ||
children.translated_text: If he should wish, 'May I take away his food-power,'

children.text: ādadīyeti tasya sabhāyām uttāno nipadya bhuvanasya pata iti tṛṇāni saṃgṛhṇīyāt prajāpatir vai bhuvanasya patiḥ prajāpatinaivāsyānnādyam ādatta idam aham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasyānnādyaṃ harāmīty āhānnādyam evāsya harati ṣaḍbhir harati ṣaḍ vā ṛtavaḥ prajāpatinaivāsyānnādyam ādāyartavo 'smā anuprayacchanti ||
children.translated_text: then, lying on his back in that man's assembly, he should gather grasses with the words, 'Of the lord of the world.' <s>Prajāpati</s> is the lord of the world; by <s>Prajāpati</s> he takes away that man's food-power. He says, 'Here I take away the food-power of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.' He indeed takes away his food-power. He takes it with six formulas; six indeed are the seasons. Having taken his food-power by <s>Prajāpati</s>, the seasons hand it over to him.

children.text: yo jyeṣṭhabandhur apabhūtaḥ syāt taṃ sthale 'vasāyya brahmaudanaṃ catuḥśarāvam paktvā tasmai hotavyā varṣma vai rāṣṭrabhṛto varṣma sthalaṃ varṣmaṇaivainaṃ varṣma samānānāṃ gamayati catuḥśarāvo bhavati dikṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati kṣīre bhavati rucaṃ evāsmin dadhāty uddharati śṛtatvāya sarpiṣvān bhavati medhyatvāya catvāra ārṣeyāḥ prāśnanti diśām eva jyotiṣi juhoti ||
children.translated_text: If an elder kinsman has been deprived of his position, one should set him down on high ground, cook a brahmaudana of four dishes, and make offerings for him. The Rāṣṭrabhṛts are eminence; high ground is eminence. By eminence he brings him to eminence among his equals. It has four dishes; he is established in the directions. It is in milk; he places brilliance in him. He lifts it out for its being well-cooked. It contains ghee, for purity. Four descendants of seers eat it; he offers into the lights of the directions.

children.text: Chapter 5
ayam puro harikeśaḥ sūryaraśmis tasya rathagṛtsaś ca rathaujāś ca senānigrāmaṇyau puñjikasthalā ca kṛtasthalā cāpsarasau yātudhānā hetī rakṣāṃsi prahetiḥ
children.translated_text: This one in front is <s>Harikeśa</s>, the sunbeam; his army-leaders and village-leaders are <s>Rathagṛtsa</s> and <s>Rathaujā</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are <s>Puñjikasthalā</s> and <s>Kṛtasthalā</s>; the yātudhānas are his missile, and the rakṣases his counter-missile.

children.text: ayaṃ dakṣiṇā viśvakarmā tasya rathasvanaś ca rathecitraś ca senānigrāmaṇyau menakā ca sahajanyā cāpsarasau daṅkṣṇavaḥ paśavo hetiḥ pauruṣeyo vadhaḥ prahetiḥ
children.translated_text: This one on the south is <s>Viśvakarman</s>; his army-leaders and village-leaders are <s>Rathasvana</s> and <s>Rathecitra</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are <s>Menakā</s> and <s>Sahajanyā</s>; biting beasts are his missile, and death by men his counter-missile.

children.text: ayam paścād viśvavyacās tasya ratheprotaś cāsamarathaś ca senānigrāmaṇyau pramlocantī ca ||
children.translated_text: This one behind is <s>Viśvavyacas</s>; his army-leaders and village-leaders are <s>Ratheprota</s> and <s>Asamaratha</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are <s>Pramlocantī</s> and

children.text: anumlocantī cāpsarasau sarpā hetir vyāghrāḥ prahetiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anumlocantī</s>; serpents are his missile, and tigers his counter-missile.

children.text: ayam uttarāt saṃyadvasus tasya senajic ca suṣeṇaś ca senānigrāmaṇyau viśvācī ca ghṛtācī cāpsarasāv āpo hetir vātaḥ prahetiḥ
children.translated_text: This one on the north is <s>Saṃyadvasu</s>; his army-leaders and village-leaders are <s>Senajit</s> and <s>Suṣeṇa</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are <s>Viśvācī</s> and <s>Ghṛtācī</s>; waters are his missile, and wind his counter-missile.

children.text: ayam upary arvāgvasus tasya tārkṣyaś cāriṣṭanemiś ca senānigrāmaṇyāv urvaśī ca pūrvacittiś cāpsarasau vidyuddhetir avasphūrjan prahetis tebhyo namas te no mṛḍayantu te yam ||
children.translated_text: This one above is <s>Arvāgvasu</s>; his army-leaders and village-leaders are <s>Tārkṣya</s> and <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are <s>Urvaśī</s> and <s>Pūrvacitti</s>; lightning is his missile, and thunder his counter-missile. Homage to them; may they be gracious to us. The one whom

children.text: dviṣmo yaś ca no dveṣṭi taṃ vo jambhe dadhāmi
children.translated_text: we hate and the one who hates us, I place him in your jaws.

children.text: āyos tvā sadane sādayāmy avataś chāyāyāṃ namaḥ samudrāya namaḥ samudrasya cakṣase
children.translated_text: I set you down in the seat of <s>Āyu</s>, in the shadow of the pit. Homage to the ocean; homage to the eye of the ocean.

children.text: parameṣṭhī tvā sādayatu divaḥ pṛṣṭhe vyacasvatīm prathasvatīṃ vibhūmatīm prabhūmatīm paribhūmatīṃ divaṃ yaccha divaṃ dṛṃha divam mā hiṃsīr viśvasmai prāṇāyāpānāya vyānāyodānāya pratiṣṭhāyai caritrāya sūryas tvābhi pātu mahyā svastyā chardiṣā śaṃtamena tayā devatayāṅgirasvad dhruvā sīda
children.translated_text: May <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> set you down on the back of heaven, wide, broad, far-extending, mighty, all-encompassing. Hold heaven; strengthen heaven; do not harm heaven. For all breath, out-breath, diffused breath, up-breath, stability, and movement, may the sun protect you with great well-being and with the most peaceful shelter. With that deity, like an <s>Aṅgiras</s>, sit firm.

children.text: prothad aśvo na yavase aviṣyan yadā mahaḥ saṃvaraṇād vyasthāt
children.translated_text: The horse neighed like one longing for barley, when he stood apart from the great enclosure.

children.text: ād asya vāto anu vāti śocir adha sma te vrajanaṃ kṛṣṇam asti ||
children.translated_text: Then the wind blows after his flame; and thereafter your pen is dark.

children.text: Chapter 6
namas te rudra manyava uto ta iṣave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to your wrath, <s>Rudra</s>, and homage also to your arrow.

children.text: namas te astu dhanvane bāhubhyām uta te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage be to your bow, and homage also to your two arms.

children.text: yā ta iṣuḥ śivatamā śivam babhūva te dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: That arrow of yours which is most auspicious, and your bow which has become auspicious,

children.text: śivā śaravyā yā tava tayā no rudra mṛḍaya ||
children.translated_text: and that quiver of yours which is auspicious: with that, <s>Rudra</s>, be gracious to us.

children.text: yā te rudra śivā tanūr aghorāpāpakāśinī
children.translated_text: That auspicious body of yours, <s>Rudra</s>, not terrible and showing no evil,

children.text: tayā nas tanuvā śaṃtamayā giriśantābhi cākaśīhi ||
children.translated_text: with that most peaceful body, O mountain-dweller, look upon us.

children.text: yām iṣuṃ giriśanta haste ||
children.translated_text: The arrow which, O mountain-dweller, in your hand

children.text: bibharṣy astave
children.translated_text: you bear to shoot,

children.text: śivāṃ giritra tāṃ kuru mā hiṃsīḥ puruṣaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: make that auspicious, O lord of the mountain; do not harm man or world.

children.text: śivena vacasā tvā giriśācchāvadāmasi
children.translated_text: With auspicious speech we address you, O mountain-dweller,

children.text: yathā naḥ sarvam ij jagad ayakṣmaṃ sumanā asat ||
children.translated_text: so that this whole world of ours may be free from disease and well-disposed.

children.text: adhyavocad adhivaktā prathamo daivyo bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The advocate has spoken forth, the first divine physician,

children.text: ahīṃś ca sarvāñjambhayant sarvāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: crushing all serpents and all yātudhānī demons.

children.text: asau yas tāmro aruṇa uta babhruḥ sumaṅgalaḥ
children.translated_text: That one there who is copper-red, ruddy, and also tawny, very auspicious,

children.text: ye cemāṃ rudrā abhito dikṣu ||
children.translated_text: and those <s>Rudras</s> who all around this

children.text: śritāḥ sahasraśo 'vaiṣāṃ heḍa īmahe ||
children.translated_text: are stationed in the directions by the thousands: we seek to avert their wrath.

children.text: asau yo 'vasarpati nīlagrīvo vilohitaḥ
children.translated_text: That one there who glides downward, blue-necked and red-hued

children.text: utainaṃ gopā adṛśann adṛśann udahāryaḥ
children.translated_text: And the cowherds saw him; the water-carriers saw him.

children.text: utainaṃ viśvā bhūtāni sa dṛṣṭo mṛḍayāti naḥ ||
children.translated_text: And all beings saw him; having been seen, may he show favor to us.

children.text: namo astu nīlagrīvāya sahasrākṣāya mīḍhuṣe
children.translated_text: Homage be to the blue-necked, thousand-eyed, bountiful one.

children.text: atho ye asya satvāno 'haṃ tebhyo 'karaṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whatever attendants are his, I have made homage to them.

children.text: pra muñca dhanvanas tvam ubhayor ārtniyor jyām
children.translated_text: Release, you, the bowstring from both ends of your bow.

children.text: yāś ca te hasta iṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the arrows that are in your hand,

children.text: parā tā bhagavo vapa ||
children.translated_text: cast them away, O blessed one.

children.text: avatatya dhanus tvaṃ sahasrākṣa śateṣudhe
children.translated_text: Having unstrung your bow, O thousand-eyed one, O possessor of a hundred quivers,

children.text: niśīrya śalyānām mukhā śivo naḥ sumanā bhava ||
children.translated_text: having broken off the points of the arrows, be auspicious and kindly disposed to us.

children.text: vijyaṃ dhanuḥ kapardino viśalyo bāṇavāṁ uta
children.translated_text: Let the bow of the braided-haired one be stringless, and let his arrow-bearing bow be without arrow-heads too.

children.text: aneśann asyeṣava ābhur asya niṣaṅgathiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let his arrows disappear; let his quiver become empty.

children.text: yā te hetir mīḍhuṣṭama haste babhūva te dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: That missile of yours, O most bountiful one, which has become the bow in your hand,

children.text: tayāsmān viśvatas tvam ayakṣmayā paribhuja ||
children.translated_text: with that, free from disease, protect us on every side.

children.text: namas te astv āyudhāyānātatāya dhṛṣṇave
children.translated_text: Homage be to your weapon, unstrung yet bold,

children.text: ubhābhyām uta te namo bāhubhyāṃ tava dhanvane ||
children.translated_text: and homage to both your arms and to your bow.

children.text: pari te dhanvano hetir asmān vṛṇaktu viśvataḥ
children.translated_text: May the missile of your bow avoid us on every side.

children.text: atho ya iṣudhis tavāre asman nidhehi tam ||
children.translated_text: And place that quiver of yours far away from us.

children.text: Chapter 7
namo hiraṇyabāhave senānye diśāṃ ca pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the golden-armed commander and lord of the quarters; homage.

children.text: namo vṛkṣebhyo harikeśebhyaḥ paśūnām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the trees with green hair, to the lord of cattle; homage.

children.text: namaḥ saspiñjarāya tviṣīmate pathīnām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the tawny one, the radiant one, to the lord of paths; homage.

children.text: namo babhluśāya vivyādhine 'nnānām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the brown one, the piercer, to the lord of foods; homage.

children.text: namo harikeśāyopavītine puṣṭānām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the green-haired one wearing the sacred thread, to the lord of the well-nourished; homage.

children.text: namo bhavasya hetyai jagatām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the missile of <s>Bhava</s>, to the lord of moving beings; homage.

children.text: namo rudrāyātatāvine kṣetrāṇām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Rudra</s> with drawn bow, to the lord of fields; homage.

children.text: namaḥ sūtāyāhantyāya vanānām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the charioteer, the striker, to the lord of forests; homage.

children.text: namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage.

children.text: rohitāya sthapataye vṛkṣāṇām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the red one, the master-builder, to the lord of trees; homage.

children.text: namo mantriṇe vāṇijāya kakṣāṇām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the counsellor, the merchant, to the lord of thickets; homage.

children.text: namo bhuvantaye vārivaskṛtāyauṣadhīnām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the prospering one, the preparer of room, to the lord of herbs; homage.

children.text: nama uccairghoṣāyākrandayate pattīnām pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the loud-shouting one, the one who makes cry out, to the lord of foot-soldiers; homage.

children.text: namaḥ kṛtsnavītāya dhāvate satvanām pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the all-encompassing one who runs, to the lord of warriors; homage.

children.text: Chapter 8
ṛksāme vai devebhyo yajñāyātiṣṭhamāne kṛṣṇo rūpaṃ kṛtvāpakramyātiṣṭhatām
children.translated_text: When the <s>Ṛc</s> and the <s>Sāman</s>, standing firm for the sacrifice for the gods, had taken on a black form and gone away, they remained apart.

children.text: te 'manyanta
children.translated_text: They thought,

children.text: yaṃ vā ime upāvartsyataḥ sa idaṃ bhaviṣyatīti te upāmantrayant te ahorātrayor mahimānam apanidhāya devān upāvartetām
children.translated_text: 'Whichever one these two turn toward, he will become this.' They invited them, and the two, having laid aside the greatness of day and night, turned toward the gods.

children.text: eṣa vā ṛco varṇo yacchuklaṃ kṛṣṇājinasya
children.translated_text: This is the color of the <s>Ṛc</s>, namely what is white on the black antelope skin.

children.text: eṣa sāmno yatkṛṣṇam
children.translated_text: This is that of the <s>Sāman</s>, namely what is black.

children.text: ṛksāmayoḥ śilpe stha ity āha
children.translated_text: He says, 'You are the forms of the <s>Ṛc</s> and the <s>Sāman</s>.'

children.text: ṛksāme evāvarunddhe
children.translated_text: He thereby secures the <s>Ṛc</s> and the <s>Sāman</s> themselves.

children.text: eṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed

children.text: vā ahno varṇo yac chuklaṃ kṛṣṇājinasyaiṣa rātriyā yat kṛṣṇaṃ yad evainayos tatra nyaktaṃ tad evāva runddhe
children.translated_text: is the color of day, namely what is white on the black antelope skin; this is that of night, namely what is black. Whatever of these two is marked there, that very thing he secures.

children.text: kṛṣṇājinena dīṣayati brahmaṇo vā etad rūpaṃ yat kṛṣṇājinam brahmaṇaivainaṃ dīkṣayati
children.translated_text: He initiates him with a black antelope skin. This, namely the black antelope skin, is the form of <s>brahman</s>; with <s>brahman</s> itself he initiates him.

children.text: imāṃ dhiyam śikṣamāṇasya devety āha yathāyajur evaitat
children.translated_text: He says, 'This thought of the one being instructed, O god'; this is just as in the <s>yajus</s> formula.

children.text: garbho vā eṣa yad dīkṣita ulbaṃ vāsaḥ prorṇute tasmāt ||
children.translated_text: The initiated man is an embryo; the garment is the caul. He wraps himself up. Therefore

children.text: garbhāḥ prāvṛtā jāyante
children.translated_text: embryos are born covered.

children.text: na purā somasya krayād aporṇvīta yat purā somasya krayād aporṇvīta garbhāḥ prajānām parāpātukāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: He should not uncover himself before the purchase of <s>Soma</s>. If he were to uncover himself before the purchase of <s>Soma</s>, the embryos of creatures would be liable to fall away.

children.text: krīte some 'porṇute jāyata eva tad atho yathā vasīyāmsam pratyaporṇute tādṛg eva tat
children.translated_text: When <s>Soma</s> has been bought, he uncovers himself; thereby he is truly born. And further, just as one uncovers himself before a better garment, so it is.

children.text: aṅgirasaḥ suvargaṃ lokaṃ yanta ūrjaṃ vy abhajanta tato yad atyaśiṣyata te śarā abhavann ūrg vai śarā yaccharamayī ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Aṅgirases</s> were going to the heavenly world, they divided vigor. What was left over became reeds. Vigor indeed is reeds, since

children.text: mekhalā bhavaty ūrjam evāva runddhe
children.translated_text: the girdle is made of reed; he thereby secures vigor.

children.text: madhyataḥ saṃ nahyati madhyata evāsmā ūrjaṃ dadhāti tasmān madhyata ūrjā bhuñjate
children.translated_text: He binds it around the middle; from the middle itself he places vigor in him. Therefore people enjoy food by means of the vigor in the middle.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ vai puruṣasya nābhyai medhyam avācīnam amedhyaṃ yan madhyataḥ saṃnahyati medhyaṃ caivāsyāmedhyaṃ ca vyāvartayati
children.translated_text: What is above a man's navel is fit for sacrifice, what is below is unfit. When he binds it around the middle, he separates in him what is fit for sacrifice and what is unfit.

children.text: indro vṛtrāya vajram prāharat sa tredhā vy abhavat sphyas tṛtīyam rathas tṛtīyaṃ yūpas tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> hurled the thunderbolt at <s>Vṛtra</s>. It became divided in three: one third the wooden sword, one third the chariot, one third the sacrificial post.

children.text: ye 'ntaḥśarā aśīryanta te śarā abhavan tac charāṇāṃ śaratvam
children.translated_text: The inner reeds that splintered became reeds; that is the reedhood of reeds.

children.text: vajro vai śarāḥ kṣut khalu vai manuṣyasya bhrātṛvyo yac charamayī mekhalā bhavati vajreṇaiva sākṣāt kṣudham bhrātṛvyam madhyato 'pahate
children.translated_text: Reeds are the thunderbolt. Hunger, surely, is a man's rival. When the girdle is made of reed, with the thunderbolt itself he strikes hunger, his rival, away from the middle.

children.text: trivṛd bhavati trivṛd vai prāṇas trivṛtam eva prāṇam madhyato yajamāne dadhāti
children.translated_text: It is threefold; the breath is threefold. He thus places the threefold breath in the sacrificer from the middle.

children.text: pṛthvī bhavati rajjūnāṃ vyāvṛttyai
children.translated_text: It is broad, for the separation of the cords.

children.text: mekhalayā yajamānaṃ dīkṣayati yoktreṇa patnīm mithunatvāya ||
children.translated_text: With the girdle he initiates the sacrificer; with the yoke-rope, the wife, for the sake of pairing.

children.text: yajño dakṣiṇām abhyadhyāyat
children.translated_text: The sacrifice brooded over the sacrificial fee.

children.text: tāṃ samabhavat
children.translated_text: He united with her.

children.text: tad indro 'cāyat
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> perceived that.

children.text: so 'manyata yo vā ito janiṣyate sa idam bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: He thought, 'Whoever will be born from her here will become this.'

children.text: tām prāviśat
children.translated_text: He entered her.

children.text: tasyā indra evājāyata
children.translated_text: From her <s>Indra</s> himself was born.

children.text: so 'manyata
children.translated_text: He thought,

children.text: yo vai mad ito 'paro janiṣyate sa idam bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: 'Whoever will be born from me here after this will become this.'

children.text: tasyā anumṛśya yonim ācchinat
children.translated_text: After touching her womb, he cut it off.

children.text: sā sūtavaśābhavat
children.translated_text: She became a female that had already calved.

children.text: tat sūtavaśāyai janma ||
children.translated_text: That is the birth of the sūtavaśā cow.

children.text: tāṃ haste nyaveṣṭayata
children.translated_text: He wrapped it around his hand.

children.text: tām mṛgeṣu nyadadhāt
children.translated_text: He placed it among the wild animals.

children.text: sā kṛṣṇaviṣāṇābhavat
children.translated_text: It became the black antelope horn.

children.text: indrasya yonir asi mā mā hiṃsīr iti kṛṣṇaviṣāṇām prayacchati
children.translated_text: He gives the black antelope horn, saying, 'You are <s>Indra</s>'s womb; do not harm me.'

children.text: sayonim eva yajñaṃ karoti sayoniṃ dakṣiṇāṃ sayonim indraṃ sayonitvāya
children.translated_text: He thereby makes the sacrifice possessed of its womb, the sacrificial fee possessed of its womb, and <s>Indra</s> possessed of his womb, for the sake of having a womb.

children.text: kṛṣyai tvā susasyāyā ity āha tasmād akṛṣṭapacyā oṣadhayaḥ pacyante
children.translated_text: He says, 'For ploughing I take you, for good crops.' Therefore plants that ripen without ploughing are ripened.

children.text: supippalābhyas tvauṣadhībhya ity āha tasmād oṣadhayaḥ phalaṃ gṛhṇanti
children.translated_text: He says, "For you, for the plants with good fruits"; therefore the plants take on fruit.

children.text: yaddhastena ||
children.translated_text: If with the hand

children.text: kaṇḍūyeta pāmanambhāvukāḥ prajāḥ syur yat smayeta nagnambhāvukāḥ
children.translated_text: he were to scratch himself, his offspring would become affected with itch; if he were to smile, they would become naked.

children.text: kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā kaṇḍūyate 'pigṛhya smayate prajānāṃ gopīthāya
children.translated_text: He scratches himself with the black antelope horn, and he smiles while covering himself, for the protection of his offspring.

children.text: na purā dakṣiṇābhyo netoḥ kṛṣṇaviṣāṇām avacṛted yat purā dakṣiṇābhyo netoḥ kṛṣṇaviṣāṇām avacṛted yoniḥ prajānām parāpātukā syāt
children.translated_text: Before the sacrificial gifts have been led away, he should not cut off the black antelope horn. If he were to cut off the black antelope horn before the gifts have been led away, the womb of his offspring would fall away.

children.text: nītāsu dakṣiṇāsu cātvāle kṛṣṇaviṣāṇām prāsyati yonir vai yajñasya cātvālaṃ yoniḥ kṛṣṇaviṣāṇā yonāv eva yoniṃ dadhāti yajñasya sayonitvāya ||
children.translated_text: When the sacrificial gifts have been led away, he throws the black antelope horn into the cātvāla pit. The cātvāla is the womb of the sacrifice, and the black antelope horn is a womb; he places womb in womb, so that the sacrifice may have its proper womb.

children.text: Chapter 9
ghnanti vā etat somaṃ yad abhiṣuṇvanti
children.translated_text: They do, in effect, kill <s>Soma</s> when they press him.

children.text: yat saumyo bhavati yathā mṛtāyānustaraṇīṃ ghnanti tādṛg eva tat
children.translated_text: When the Saumya offering is made, it is just like killing the covering cow for a dead man.

children.text: yad uttarārdhe vā madhye vā juhuyāt devatābhyaḥ samadaṃ dadhyād dakṣiṇārdhe juhoty eṣā vai pitṝṇāṃ dik svāyām eva diśi pitṝn niravadayate
children.translated_text: If he were to offer in the northern half or in the middle, he would create conflict with the deities. He offers in the southern half; that indeed is the direction of the Fathers. In their own direction he thus sets the Fathers apart.

children.text: udgātṛbhyo haranti sāmadaivatyo vai saumyo yad eva sāmnaś chambaṭkurvanti tasyaiva sa śāntiḥ
children.translated_text: They carry it to the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests. The Saumya belongs to the deity of the sāman; whatever they injure in the sāman,

children.text: ava ||
children.translated_text: of that it is the appeasement.

children.text: īkṣante pavitraṃ vai saumya ātmānam eva pavayante
children.translated_text: They look down. The Saumya is a purifier; they purify themselves.

children.text: ya ātmānaṃ na paripaśyed itāsuḥ syād abhidadiṃ kṛtvāvekṣeta tasmin hy ātmānam paripaśyaty atho ātmānam eva pavayate
children.translated_text: If one did not see himself, he would become lifeless. He should look after making an opening, for in it he sees himself; and further, he purifies himself.

children.text: yo gatamanāḥ syāt so 'vekṣeta yan me manaḥ parāgataṃ yad vā me aparāgatam
children.translated_text: One whose mind has gone away should look, saying, "Whatever mind of mine has gone away, or whatever has not come back to me,

children.text: rājñā somena tad vayam asmāsu dhārayāmasīti mana evātman dādhāra ||
children.translated_text: that, with king <s>Soma</s>, we hold fast in ourselves." Thus he has placed the mind in the self.

children.text: na gatamanā bhavati
children.translated_text: He does not become one whose mind has gone away.

children.text: apa vai tṛtīyasavane yajñaḥ krāmatījānād anījānam abhy āgnāvaiṣṇavyarcā ghṛtasya yajaty agniḥ sarvā devatā viṣṇur yajño devatāś caiva yajñaṃ ca dādhāra
children.translated_text: At the third pressing the sacrifice goes away from the one who has sacrificed toward the one who has not sacrificed. He offers ghee with a verse to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>. <s>Agni</s> is all the deities, and <s>Vishnu</s> is the sacrifice; he has thereby upheld both the deities and the sacrifice.

children.text: upāmśu yajati mithunatvāya
children.translated_text: He sacrifices silently, for the sake of pairing.

children.text: brahmavādino vadanti mitro yajñasya sviṣṭaṃ yuvate varuṇo duriṣṭaṃ kva tarhi yajñaḥ kva yajamāno bhavatīti yan maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām ālabhate mitreṇaiva ||
children.translated_text: The theologians say, "<s>Mitra</s> takes away what is well offered in the sacrifice, and <s>Varuṇa</s> what is badly offered. Where then is the sacrifice, where is the sacrificer?" When he seizes a Maitrāvaruṇa barren cow, by <s>Mitra</s>

children.text: yajñasya sviṣṭaṃ śamayati varuṇena duriṣṭaṃ nārtim ārchati yajamānas
children.translated_text: he appeases what is well offered in the sacrifice, and by <s>Varuṇa</s> what is badly offered. The sacrificer does not incur misfortune.

children.text: yathā vai lāṅgaleno 'rvarām prabhindanty evam ṛksāme yajñam pra bhintto yan maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām ālabhate yajñāyaiva prabhinnāya matyam anvavāsyati śāntyai
children.translated_text: Just as they break open uncultivated ground with a plough, so the ṛc and sāman break open the sacrifice. When he seizes a Maitrāvaruṇa barren cow, he places a prop alongside the sacrifice that has been broken open, for appeasement.

children.text: yātayāmāni vā etasya chandāṃsi ya ījānaś chandasām eṣa raso yad vaśā yan maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām ālabhate chandāṃsy eva punar ā prīṇāty ayātayāmatvāyātho chandaḥsv eva rasaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The metres of one who has sacrificed are, as it were, worn out. The barren cow is the essence of the metres. When he seizes a Maitrāvaruṇa barren cow, he refreshes the metres again, so that they may not be worn out; and further, he places essence in the metres themselves.
